D.intro: Section D proves that every person doing the work knows the hazards, has been trained for the job they actually do, and holds any licence or permit the work needs. It starts from a training needs analysis per job role, is tracked in one training matrix, and is backed by the certificates, induction records and toolbox talk registers themselves.
what_goes_here: A training needs analysis listing what each job role must be trained in
A training matrix showing every person, every required course, the date done, the expiry date and where the proof is
Signed induction records for employees, contractors and visitors
Certificates for statutory and safety critical courses such as first aid, fire fighting and health and safety representative training
Copies of licences and permits held by people, such as professional driving permits and operator certificates
Toolbox talk registers with attendance signatures, and competency assessment records
first_file_tips: Do the training needs analysis first, from your risk assessment in Section C; it stops you paying for courses nobody needs and missing the ones the work demands.
Build the matrix in one spreadsheet before chasing certificates, then fill the gaps oldest expiry first.
Keep a clear copy of every certificate and licence, front and back, and write the expiry date on the matrix, not only on the card.

No competent person in house to assess risk, train people or sign competency assessments? Care Net's Recruitment Portal places and onboards one, with the appointment and engagement letters your File needs; use the recruitment button on Section B or on the File header, which puts you in touch with a sales executive until the portal address is live.

E.intro: Section E shows that people are fit for the work and exposures your risk assessment found, and that their health information is handled confidentially. Its key document is your Medical Surveillance Plan, a separate Care Net product signed by the occupational medical practitioner (OMP), and this section is signed off by the OMP only. Care Net screens fitness for work and does not diagnose. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; your File holds only the outcome for each person: fit, fit with restrictions or unfit.
what_goes_here: The released Medical Surveillance Plan, a separate Care Net product signed by the OMP
Certificates of fitness per employee: baseline, periodic and exit
Construction, driving permit and mine fitness certificates where that work applies
Outcomes of the specific examinations your exposures call for, such as lead, noise or hazardous chemical agents
A register of fitness restrictions and how each one was reflected in the person's job
Proof that occupational diseases were reported (date, body notified and reference), first aid records and a note on how medical records are kept confidential
first_file_tips: Finish your risk assessment in Section C first; the Medical Surveillance Plan, a separate Care Net product signed by the OMP, is built from the exposures it finds, not from job titles.
Never upload clinical notes, test results or doctors' letters to your File. Upload only the certificate of fitness showing the outcome.
Put each person's certificate expiry date in your training and medical diary so nobody works past it.
If a certificate says fit with restrictions, record what you changed in the person's job; that record matters as much as the certificate.

what_to_submit: Training needs analysis listing each job role and the training it requires
The risk assessment or job descriptions it was built from
Signature and date of your section 16(2) assignee approving it
HSF-D-01.why: It links the hazards in your risk assessment to the training each role needs, so nobody is sent to work untrained and you do not pay for courses that do not fit the job. Your section 16(2) assignee reviews it once a year and whenever a role, process or piece of equipment changes.
HSF-D-01.example: Example: Sithole Precast in Brits lists five roles; the batching plant operator needs forklift, hazardous chemical handling and hearing conservation training, while the yard cleaner needs induction, ergonomics and emergency evacuation.
common_gaps: Listing people instead of roles, so the analysis breaks when staff change
Copying a generic course list that ignores your own risk assessment
Forgetting supervisors, appointees and office staff who visit the floor

what_to_submit: Training matrix naming every person, each required course, date completed and expiry date
A reference to where each certificate is filed
A monthly sign off or date stamp showing the matrix was checked
HSF-D-02.why: The matrix is the one page an inspector, auditor or client looks at to see whether your people are trained and in date. Checking it every month lets you book refresher training before a certificate lapses; where Care Net delivered the training, the record can arrive from MyClinicOnline once it is connected.
HSF-D-02.example: Example: Mokoena Logistics in Germiston keeps a matrix of its 34 staff; in the June check the safety officer, Lerato Dlamini, flags two forklift certificates expiring and books the refresher before month end.
common_gaps: A matrix with no expiry column, so lapses go unnoticed
New starters added to payroll but not to the matrix
Entries marked done with no certificate on file to prove it

what_to_submit: Signed induction record for each employee, with the date and the modules covered
Contractor induction records before they start work on site
Visitor register or visitor induction slip showing site rules were explained
HSF-D-03.why: Induction is where every person first learns the hazards, the emergency route and how to report a problem, so it protects people from day one. An inspector will often pick names from your staff list and ask to see their induction record; complete one each time a new person, contractor or visitor arrives.
HSF-D-03.example: Example: Naidoo Food Packers in Pinetown inducts new packer Sipho Zulu on his first morning; he initials the modules on noise zones, chemical labels and the evacuation route, and his supervisor countersigns.
common_gaps: Inducting in a language or way the person cannot follow
No induction for contractors or temporary workers
Records without the employee's own signature

what_to_submit: Certificate of each statutory or safety critical course, per person
Attendance register or provider confirmation for group training
Training provider's accreditation or the trainer's credentials
Matrix entry showing the expiry date
HSF-D-04.why: These courses are what the risk assessment and your appointments rely on: without them first aiders, representatives and operators are named on paper but not able to act. Renew each one before the certificate expires; where Care Net delivered the course the record can come from MyClinicOnline once it is connected.
HSF-D-04.example: Example: Botha Steel Fabricators in Vanderbijlpark files its fire fighting, first aid and working at height certificates per person, each cross referenced to its training matrix.
common_gaps: Keeping certificates for people who have left while current staff have none
Accepting certificates from providers you cannot verify
Letting refresher dates slip because nobody owns the diary

what_to_submit: Clear copy of each licence, permit or registration card, front and back
A record of the date you checked it was valid
Matrix entry showing the expiry date
HSF-D-05.why: Some work may only be done by a person who holds a licence, permit or registration, and an incident involving an unlicensed person is hard to defend to an inspector, client or insurer. Check each one before the person starts and renew it before it expires.
HSF-D-05.example: Example: Khoza Transport in Polokwane copies each driver's licence and professional driving permit on the first working day of the month and notes the expiry dates on its matrix.
common_gaps: Copying the licence once at hiring and never checking it again
No licence on file for relief or temporary operators

what_to_submit: Toolbox talk register with topic, date, presenter and attendee signatures
The short talk notes or handout used
Any action raised during the talk and who followed it up
HSF-D-06.why: Short regular talks keep hazards front of mind and show that you keep informing people after induction, especially after an incident or a change. Your supervisor records each talk as it happens; auditors look for talks that match your real risks and recent incidents.
HSF-D-06.example: Example: Pillay Plumbing's supervisor in Durban runs a Monday talk on trench collapse after a near miss, and six workers sign the register.
common_gaps: The same talk repeated every week regardless of what is happening on site
Registers signed by people who were not there
No link between talks and recent incidents or new hazards

what_to_submit: Competency assessment record per person, naming the task and the outcome
The assessor's name and credentials
Any observation checklist or practical test used
HSF-D-07.why: Some roles need proof that a person can actually do the task safely, not only that they sat in a class. A signed assessment shows the person was watched doing the work and judged competent; reassess before the assessment expires or when the task changes.
HSF-D-07.example: Example: Mathebula Mining Supplies in Rustenburg has its workshop foreman, a qualified assessor, watch forklift operator Neo Molefe complete a practical route and signs him competent, filing the checklist.
common_gaps: Treating an attendance certificate as proof of competence
Assessments signed by someone who is not competent to assess
No reassessment after a person returns from long absence

what_to_submit: The released Medical Surveillance Plan, a separate Care Net product signed by the OMP
The list of exposure groups and jobs the Plan covers
Record of the yearly review and any changes
HSF-E-01.why: The Plan is Section E's key evidence: it sets out which people need which examinations, based on the exposures your risk assessment found. It is a separate Care Net product signed by the occupational medical practitioner, and it is reviewed once a year and whenever your exposures change.
HSF-E-01.example: Example: Ndlovu Engineering in Middelburg files its Medical Surveillance Plan, a separate Care Net product signed by its OMP,, covering welders for noise and fumes and stores staff for manual handling only.
common_gaps: A Plan copied from another company that does not match your exposures
An unsigned draft filed as the final Plan
No review after a new process or chemical is introduced

what_to_submit: Certificate of fitness per employee showing the outcome: fit, fit with restrictions or unfit
Baseline certificate for new starters, periodic certificates, and exit certificates for leavers
The Plan protocol or exposure group each certificate relates to
HSF-E-02.why: Certificates show that each person was screened against the exposures in the Plan before and while doing the work. Care Net screens fitness for work and does not diagnose; clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner and only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File, renewed before each certificate expires.
HSF-E-02.example: Example: Molefe Bricks in Brakpan files a baseline certificate for new kiln operator Themba Mahlangu marked fit, and an exit certificate for a retiring operator marked fit, with no clinical notes attached.
common_gaps: Filing clinical results or doctors' letters in the File
No exit certificates, so later disease claims cannot be traced to a start point
Letting certificates expire while the person keeps working

what_to_submit: Construction medical certificate of fitness for each person working on the site
A site list matching each worker to a current certificate
Certificates for contractors' workers, obtained from each contractor
HSF-E-03.why: The Construction Regulations, 2014 expect workers on a construction site to have a valid medical certificate of fitness for the work they do, and the principal contractor checks this at the gate. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Renew each certificate before it expires.
HSF-E-03.example: Example: Shabangu Civils in Emalahleni keeps a site list for a road upgrade that ticks each of its 22 workers against a current construction certificate of fitness from Care Net.
common_gaps: Allowing a worker on site while the certificate is being renewed
Not collecting certificates from subcontractors
Certificates that do not state the type of work assessed, such as work at height

what_to_submit: Fitness outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) for each professional driving permit holder
Copy of the driver's current professional driving permit
A diary of permit and fitness expiry dates
HSF-E-04.why: A professional driving permit needs a medical fitness declaration, and a driver who becomes unfit puts other road users at risk. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Keep the fitness outcome with the permit copy and renew both before they expire.
HSF-E-04.example: Example: Venter Bus Services in Bloemfontein files each driver's fitness outcome from its occupational health provider next to the permit copy, and diarises both expiry dates.
common_gaps: Filing the permit medical form itself instead of the fitness outcome
No check that relief drivers hold a current permit and fitness outcome

what_to_submit: Mine certificate of fitness for each person working at the mine
The fitness to perform work procedure or code of practice your mine follows
Access control record linking entry to a current certificate
HSF-E-05.why: Mines work under the MHSA regime, which has its own fitness requirements and codes of practice, so people must be certified fit before they go underground or into the plant. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Renew before expiry.
HSF-E-05.example: Example: Themba Drilling Contractors, working at a quarry near Kuruman, files a mine certificate of fitness for each driller and checks it against the mine's access card list.
common_gaps: Using an ordinary certificate of fitness where the mine requires its own
Contract workers entering on another company's certificate

what_to_submit: Certificate of fitness for each specific examination your exposures call for
The Plan protocol that sets the examination and how often it is done
The exposure group list showing who needs each examination
HSF-E-06.why: Certain exposures, such as lead, asbestos, hazardous chemical agents, biological agents or noise, come with their own examinations, and people must stay fit for them while exposed. The timing follows the applicable regulation and your Plan, as the OMP sets; clinical results stay with the occupational health practitioner, and only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
HSF-E-06.example: Example: Hendricks Furniture in Atlantis files noise examination outcomes for its machine shop and solvent examination outcomes for its spray team, each linked to a protocol in its Plan, while the test results stay with the occupational health practitioner.
common_gaps: Examining everyone for everything instead of by exposure
Missing the examination for workers moved into an exposed job
Filing test results instead of the fitness outcome

what_to_submit: Register of fitness restrictions with the person, the restriction as the OMP worded it and its review date
Record of how each restriction was reflected in the person's job or duties
Signed acknowledgement by the employee and supervisor
HSF-E-07.why: A restriction only protects the person if the job actually changes, and the employer may hold only what it needs to act on, not the medical reason. Record each change as it happens and review it when the certificate is renewed.
HSF-E-07.example: Example: Dube Furniture in Pinetown records that sander Mpho Kekana is fit with restrictions, no work above ladder height, and moves him to bench finishing, with both signatures.
common_gaps: Writing the diagnosis in the register instead of the restriction
Recording the restriction but not what changed in the job
Dismissing or moving a person without following a fair process

what_to_submit: Proof that each occupational disease was reported: the date, the body notified and the reference number
COIDA claim reference and the correspondence that carries no clinical detail
Actions taken in the workplace after the case
The fitness outcome only (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit); disease reports and referral letters stay with the occupational health practitioner
HSF-E-08.why: When a disease may be caused by work, it must be reported and the person referred, so they get care and compensation under COIDA and you can fix the cause. Keep a record each time it happens; the reports, referral letters and clinical details stay with the occupational health practitioner, and only the fitness outcome goes in your File.
HSF-E-08.example: Example: Radebe Panelbeaters in Soweto files the date its OMP notified a suspected occupational disease, the COIDA claim reference and the record of its spray booth ventilation repair; the report itself stays with the OMP.
common_gaps: Treating an occupational disease as a private medical matter and not reporting it
Filing the disease report or referral letter in the File
No follow up on the workplace cause

what_to_submit: Current list of first aiders per site and shift, with certificate expiry dates
Monthly first aid box inspection checklist, signed
First aid treatment register
HSF-E-09.why: Someone trained must be able to help an injured person quickly, with a stocked box, on every shift. Your appointed first aider checks the boxes every month, and the treatment register often reveals injuries nobody reported.
HSF-E-09.example: Example: Mahlaba Hardware in Mbombela has two first aiders per shift; its store manager, Zanele Mthethwa, ticks the box checklist on the last Friday of every month and replaces used plasters and gloves.
common_gaps: First aiders whose certificates have lapsed
Boxes checked but items never replaced
Night shift or weekends with no first aider on site

what_to_submit: A signed note describing which medical information the employer holds, which the occupational health practitioner holds, and why
Who in your company may see certificates of fitness and how they are stored
Your consent and privacy notice for employees
Record of the yearly review
HSF-E-10.why: Health information is sensitive, and privacy law expects you to hold only what you need, for a clear purpose, and keep it secure. The note shows that clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner and that your File holds only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit); review it once a year.
HSF-E-10.example: Example: Petersen Laundry in Paarl files a one page note: certificates of fitness sit in a locked HR cabinet and a restricted folder, clinical records stay with its occupational health provider, and only the HR officer and section 16(2) assignee may see outcomes.
common_gaps: Medical files kept in the general personnel file
Managers emailing certificates around without control
No written purpose for holding each kind of record

what_to_submit: Cholinesterase surveillance outcome per person who mixes or sprays organophosphate or carbamate pesticides: fit, fit with restrictions or unfit
Your list of spray workers and the pesticides they use
The Plan protocol for pesticide exposure, signed by the OMP
HSF-OV-AGRI-02.why: Some pesticides slow an enzyme in the blood, and surveillance picks up overexposure before a worker becomes seriously ill; the Hazardous Chemical Agents Regulations drive this for exposed farm workers. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-AGRI-02.example: Example: Van der Merwe Citrus near Citrusdal files a fit outcome for each of its six sprayers before the spraying season, and moves one to packing when the OMP records a temporary restriction.
common_gaps: Testing only after someone falls ill instead of before and during the season
Filing laboratory values instead of the outcome

what_to_submit: Chainsaw operator competency certificate per operator
Tree felling or harvesting machine competency records for forestry crews
Record of the practical assessment and the assessor's name
HSF-OV-AGRI-04.why: Chainsaws and harvesting machines cause severe cuts and crush injuries, so only people assessed as competent should operate them in the plantation. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-AGRI-04.example: Example: Shongwe Forestry Contractors near Sabie files a chainsaw competency certificate and practical assessment for each of its nine fellers.
common_gaps: Crews trained informally by a colleague with no record
Operators moved from brush cutting to felling without a new assessment

what_to_submit: Construction medical certificate of fitness for every person on the site, your own workers and contractors' workers
Site access list checked against current certificates
Contractor confirmations that their workers' certificates are current
HSF-OV-CONSTR-09.why: On a construction project the Construction Regulations, 2014 expect every person on site to be certified fit for the work they do, and the principal contractor is expected to check this for the whole site. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-CONSTR-09.example: Example: Ntuli Construction, principal contractor on a school extension in Mthatha, checks every name on its daily site register against a current certificate of fitness, including its two subcontractors' teams.
common_gaps: Checking your own workers but not subcontractors
Day labourers starting before they are assessed

what_to_submit: Fitness outcome per firefighter, traffic officer or emergency responder, against the inherent requirements of the job
The written inherent job requirements the assessment was made against
Restriction and placement record for anyone not fully fit
HSF-OV-GOV-02.why: Emergency and traffic services work is physically demanding and affects public safety, so fitness is assessed against the real demands of the job, and testing must be justified by those demands. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-GOV-02.example: Example: Lindiwe Valley Municipality, a fictitious council, files fitness outcomes for its 30 firefighters, assessed against its written firefighter job requirements.
common_gaps: Testing without written inherent job requirements to justify it
Restrictions not reflected in shift allocation

what_to_submit: Written immunisation and post exposure protocol signed by the OMP
Record per worker that immunisation was offered, with the date; acceptance, refusal and vaccination status stay with the occupational health practitioner
Post exposure incident log, such as needle stick injuries, showing the date and that it was reported, with follow up kept by the practitioner
HSF-OV-HEALTH-01.why: Healthcare and laboratory staff can catch infections from patients and samples, and the Hazardous Biological Agents Regulations expect you to protect them, including a plan for what happens straight after an exposure. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-HEALTH-01.example: Example: Kekana Family Clinic in Tzaneen files its post exposure protocol, a log showing a nurse's needle stick injury was reported the same day, and each worker's immunisation offer record.
common_gaps: No protocol for after hours exposures
Vaccination records with clinical details kept in the File

what_to_submit: Food handler fitness outcome per kitchen and service worker
Illness reporting procedure staff sign on appointment
Record of staff excluded from food handling while ill, without clinical detail
HSF-OV-HOSP-02.why: In hospitality one ill food handler can infect many guests, and the municipal environmental health practitioner will ask how you know your food handlers are fit to work. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-HOSP-02.example: Example: Mthimkhulu Guest House in Port Alfred files fitness outcomes for its cook and two kitchen assistants and a signed illness reporting procedure for each.
common_gaps: Seasonal staff starting in the kitchen before assessment
No record of who was sent home ill

what_to_submit: Forklift operator competency record per operator, naming the machine type used in your plant
Company authorisation card per operator
Periodic practical reassessment record
HSF-OV-MANU-05.why: In a factory forklifts share space with people on foot, so each operator must be competent on the specific machines and routes in your plant, not only in general. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-MANU-05.example: Example: Mathe Plastics in Isando reassesses its eight forklift operators each year on its own reach trucks and loading bay route, and renews their authorisation cards.
common_gaps: Operators trained on counterbalance forklifts driving reach trucks
Authorisation cards never withdrawn after a serious incident

what_to_submit: Your mine's written certificate of fitness procedure
Register linking each person to a current certificate of fitness
Access control rules that stop people without a current certificate
HSF-OV-MINING-10.why: Under the MHSA regime a mine runs a system to make sure nobody works without being certified fit, and inspectors look at the system, not just single certificates. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-MINING-10.example: Example: Kgosi Aggregates, a quarry near Brits, files its fitness procedure and a monthly register that its access control office uses to block expired certificates.
common_gaps: A procedure on paper that access control does not enforce
Contractors' certificates tracked outside the system

what_to_submit: PSIRA registration certificate per officer showing the grade
Your company's PSIRA registration as a security service provider
Post list showing the grade each post requires and who fills it
HSF-OV-SEC-01.why: Security work falls under the PSIRA regime, and clients check that every officer is registered and graded for the post, so an officer placed on the wrong post puts the contract and the public at risk. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-SEC-01.example: Example: Letsoalo Protection Services in Mokopane matches each of its 25 officers to a post list and moves an officer whose grade is below what the client contract asks for off the supervisor post.
common_gaps: Grade on the certificate lower than the post requires
Officers whose registration lapsed while still on duty

what_to_submit: Firearm competency certificate per armed officer for each firearm type carried
Licence for each company firearm and the safe register
Firearm issue and return register per shift
HSF-OV-SEC-02.why: Armed security work carries a risk to officers and the public, and firearms law expects competency for each firearm type and strict control of who holds which firearm. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-SEC-02.example: Example: Mabunda Cash Services in Giyani checks each armed officer's competency against the firearm issued and reconciles the safe register at every shift change.
common_gaps: Issuing a shotgun to an officer only certified for handguns
Firearms leaving the safe with no signature

what_to_submit: Rail safety critical fitness outcome per train driver, shunter or other safety critical worker
List of safety critical roles and who fills them
Restriction and removal from duty record where a person is not fit
HSF-OV-TRANS-04.why: A rail worker who is not fit for a safety critical task can cause a derailment or collision, and the rail safety regulator expects operators to manage their fitness. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-TRANS-04.example: Example: Mosia Rail Logistics in De Aar files a fit outcome for each of its locomotive drivers and shunters and removes one from duty until a restriction is reviewed.
common_gaps: Safety critical roles not listed, so people in them are missed
Returning a worker to duty before the OMP reviews a restriction

what_to_submit: Waste management licence or registration for each facility or activity that needs one
Waste manifests or safe disposal certificates for each load
Training record for staff who complete manifests and handle hazardous waste
HSF-OV-WASTE-01.why: Environmental waste law controls how waste is stored, moved and disposed of, and a missing manifest can leave you responsible for waste dumped by someone else. Staff who fill in manifests must know how. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-WASTE-01.example: Example: Ngcobo Waste Solutions in Hammarsdale files its waste licence, a manifest for each hazardous load collected, and the disposal site's safe disposal certificate that closes it off.
common_gaps: Manifests started but never closed with a disposal certificate
Licence conditions not read by the people doing the work

what_to_submit: Record per worker exposed to biological agents that immunisation was offered, with the date; acceptance, refusal and vaccination status stay with the occupational health practitioner
Your biological agent risk assessment showing who is exposed
Post exposure procedure for needle stick and sewage contact
HSF-OV-WASTE-03.why: Waste and sewage workers can be exposed to blood, needles and sewage, and the Hazardous Biological Agents Regulations expect you to protect them, including offering immunisation the practitioner recommends. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File. Review it once a year and whenever the work or the people change.
HSF-OV-WASTE-03.example: Example: Sithebe Waste Management in Hammarsdale files a dated immunisation offer record for each collection worker and its procedure for a needle found in a bag.
common_gaps: Keeping vaccination cards or refusal forms in the File instead of with the practitioner
No procedure for sharps found in general waste

what_to_submit: Health and safety representative training certificate per designated representative
Designation letter from Section B for the same person
Matrix entry with the training date
D04-01.why: Representatives inspect the workplace and raise concerns for their colleagues, and they can only do that well once trained. An inspector will ask to see both the designation and the training. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-01.example: Example: Jacobs Printing in Epping designates Fatima Adams as representative for the press floor and files her representative training certificate next to her designation letter.
common_gaps: Designating a representative and never training them
Training someone who was not elected or designated

what_to_submit: First aid certificate per first aider, with its level and expiry date
Provider's approval to train first aiders
First aider list per site and shift
D04-02.why: Trained first aiders keep an injured person alive and stable until help arrives, and you need enough of them on every shift. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-02.example: Example: Mthembu Poultry in Camperdown keeps first aid certificates for four supervisors so each of its two shifts always has two trained first aiders.
common_gaps: Certificates from a provider that is not approved to train first aiders
All first aiders on the day shift and none at night

what_to_submit: Fire fighting training certificate or attendance register per person
Content outline showing practical use of the extinguishers you actually have
D04-03.why: People who know how to use an extinguisher can stop a small fire before it spreads and know when to leave instead. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-03.example: Example: Moodley Timber in Isipingo sends eight yard staff for fire fighting training and files the provider's attendance register and certificates.
common_gaps: Training on extinguisher types you do not have on site
No practical session, only a talk

what_to_submit: Working at height and fall arrest training certificate per person
Record of harness and rescue practice
Link to the fall protection plan in Section C
D04-04.why: Falls from height are one of the most common causes of serious injury, and the Construction Regulations, 2014 expect people working at height to be trained for it. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-04.example: Example: Zwane Roofing in Kempton Park files a working at height certificate for each roofer, cross referenced to the fall protection plan for its warehouse reroof.
common_gaps: No rescue training, so nobody knows how to bring down a person hanging in a harness
Training certificates with no link to the actual fall protection plan

what_to_submit: Scaffold erector certificate for each person who erects scaffolding
Scaffold inspector certificate for the person who signs scaffolds off
Scaffold inspection register entries signed by that person
D04-05.why: A poorly built or uninspected scaffold can collapse under the people on it, so both the builders and the inspector must be competent. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-05.example: Example: Baloyi Scaffolding in Tembisa files erector certificates for its crew and an inspector certificate for foreman Kabelo Maluleke, who signs the weekly scaffold tags.
common_gaps: Scaffolds signed off by someone with only erector training
Hired scaffold with no proof of the erector's training

what_to_submit: Confined space entry training certificate per entrant, standby person and supervisor
Record of rescue drill participation
Link to the confined space permit procedure in Section G
D04-06.why: Confined spaces can hold toxic gas or too little oxygen, and many deaths are would be rescuers, so everyone involved must be trained, including the person standing by outside. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-06.example: Example: Hlongwane Water Services in Emalahleni trains a three person team in confined space entry and rescue before cleaning a municipal reservoir, and files the certificates and drill record.
common_gaps: Training the entrant but not the standby person
Gas detector training left out

what_to_submit: Operator training certificate for each person who operates a crane, hoist or lifting machine
Rigger or slinger training record for people who attach loads
Link to the lifting machine register in Section F
D04-07.why: A dropped load or overturned crane can kill people nearby, so operators and riggers must be trained on the type of machine they use. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-07.example: Example: Kruger Engineering in Vereeniging files an overhead crane operator certificate for two workshop staff and a rigging certificate for the slinger who works with them.
common_gaps: Training on one type of crane but operating another
Riggers with no training at all

what_to_submit: Forklift or mobile plant operator training certificate per operator, stating the machine type
Operator's authorisation card issued by your company
Record of the pre use check training
D04-08.why: Forklifts and mobile plant cause many workplace deaths through tipping and collisions with people on foot, so only trained, authorised operators may drive them. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-08.example: Example: Moloi Distribution in Midrand files counterbalance forklift certificates for six operators and issues each a company authorisation card after a practical check.
common_gaps: Anyone with a key allowed to drive
Certificates for a different class of machine than the one used

what_to_submit: Hazard identification and risk assessment training certificate per person who assesses risk
An example of a risk assessment that person completed
D04-09.why: Your risk assessments in Section C are only as good as the people who do them, and an inspector will ask who assessed and how they are competent. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-09.example: Example: Nel Agricultural Services in Bethlehem sends its farm manager and two supervisors on risk assessment training before they review the baseline risk assessment.
common_gaps: Risk assessments signed by people with no training at all

what_to_submit: Incident investigation training certificate per investigator
An investigation report that person completed
D04-10.why: Trained investigators find the real cause of an incident rather than blaming the injured person, so the same thing does not happen again. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-10.example: Example: Makhubu Security Services in Pretoria trains its operations manager in incident investigation, and her first report finds a broken gate light behind a guard's fall.
common_gaps: Investigations that stop at worker carelessness
Only one trained investigator for several sites

what_to_submit: Hazardous chemical handling training record per person who handles chemicals
Content covering your own safety data sheets, labels, storage and personal protective equipment
Link to your chemical inventory and hazardous chemical agent risk assessment
D04-11.why: The Hazardous Chemical Agents Regulations expect people exposed to chemicals to know the risks and controls, since chemicals can burn, poison or cause disease years later. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-11.example: Example: Mkhize Cleaning Services in Umhlanga trains its cleaners on the four chemicals they use, working through each safety data sheet and the correct gloves.
common_gaps: Generic chemical training that ignores the products you actually use
No training when a new chemical arrives

what_to_submit: Asbestos awareness training record per person who may disturb asbestos
Link to your asbestos inventory or survey where you have one
D04-12.why: Older buildings and plant may contain asbestos, and people who drill, cut or demolish without knowing can breathe in fibres that cause disease decades later. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-12.example: Example: Smit Maintenance in Kimberley trains its maintenance team in asbestos awareness before work on a school built in the 1970s, and files the attendance register.
common_gaps: Assuming asbestos is gone from all older buildings
Training staff but not subcontractors who do the drilling

what_to_submit: Lead awareness training record per person exposed to lead
Content covering hygiene, eating areas and change routines
D04-13.why: The Lead Regulations expect exposed workers to understand how lead enters the body and how hygiene and controls protect them and their families. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-13.example: Example: Mabena Radiator Works in Benoni trains its soldering staff on lead hygiene, including washing before eating and leaving work clothes at work.
common_gaps: No training for cleaners who handle lead dust
Eating allowed in the work area after training

what_to_submit: Hearing conservation training record per person working in noise zones
Record of hearing protector fit and care instruction
Link to your noise survey and zone map
D04-14.why: Noise induced hearing loss is permanent and builds slowly, so people must know where the noise zones are and how to wear protection properly. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-14.example: Example: Dlamini Sawmills in Sabie trains its mill staff on noise zones and earplug fitting, with each worker demonstrating a correct fit.
common_gaps: Issuing earplugs without showing how to fit them
Office staff who walk through noise zones left out

what_to_submit: Ergonomics training record per person in lifting, repetitive or screen based work
Link to the ergonomics risk assessment
D04-15.why: Back, neck and wrist injuries from lifting, repetitive work or poor workstations are common and costly, and simple training on safe postures prevents many of them. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-15.example: Example: Khumalo Call Centre in Durban trains its agents on chair and screen set up after its ergonomics assessment, and files the attendance register.
common_gaps: Training without changing the workstations themselves

what_to_submit: Emergency evacuation training record per person, including fire marshals
Evacuation drill report from Section H showing who took part
D04-16.why: In a fire or gas leak everyone must know the alarm, the route and the assembly point without thinking. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-16.example: Example: Maseko Office Supplies in Polokwane trains its marshals and then runs a drill; the report shows the building cleared in time and one blocked exit fixed.
common_gaps: Training marshals but never running a drill
New starters not shown the evacuation route

what_to_submit: Food handler hygiene training record per food handler
Content covering hand washing, illness reporting and cross contamination
D04-17.why: Food handlers who do not follow hygiene rules can make customers seriously ill, and your municipal environmental health practitioner will ask for proof of training. Renew it before the certificate expires; where no expiry is printed, refresh it as your risk assessment or the practitioner sets.
D04-17.example: Example: Mabuza Catering in Mbombela trains its kitchen staff in food hygiene and files the certificates next to their food handling fitness outcomes in Section E.
common_gaps: Training kitchen staff but not the people who serve or deliver food

what_to_submit: Copy of the driver's licence and professional driving permit, front and back
Date you last checked both were valid
Link to the permit medical in Section E
D05-01.why: Drivers carrying passengers, dangerous goods or heavy loads need a professional driving permit, and your insurer or client may ask for it after a crash. Check it before the person drives and renew it before it expires.
D05-01.example: Example: Mahlangu Couriers in Centurion files permit copies for its eleven truck drivers and checks them on the first of every month.
common_gaps: A permit copy with no expiry date recorded
Relief drivers driving without a permit check

what_to_submit: Operator certificate for each person operating plant or machinery, naming the machine type
Company authorisation to operate that machine
Expiry or reassessment date
D05-02.why: Plant and lifting machinery can crush or kill when misused, so only certified, authorised operators may use it. Check the certificate before the person operates and renew it before it expires.
D05-02.example: Example: Mabaso Earthworks in Kathu files a front end loader certificate and company authorisation for each of its four operators.
common_gaps: Certificates for a different machine type than the one operated
No company authorisation, so anyone certified elsewhere can drive

what_to_submit: Copy of the electrician's registration card as an electrical tester, installation electrician or master installation electrician
The electrical certificate for any installation work they signed off
Registration expiry or renewal date
D05-03.why: Only a registered person may sign off electrical installation work, and faulty electrical work causes fires and electrocution. Check registration before work starts and keep it current.
D05-03.example: Example: Nkosi Electrical Contractors in Roodepoort files the registration card of master installation electrician Busisiwe Nkosi with each certificate she issues.
common_gaps: Using an unregistered electrician because they are cheaper
Accepting a certificate with no registration number on it

what_to_submit: Copy of the gas practitioner's registration card, showing the gas type and category they may work on
Certificate of the gas installation they signed off
Registration expiry date
D05-04.why: Gas leaks and badly installed cylinders cause fires and explosions, so only a registered gas practitioner may install or alter gas systems. Check the registration category matches the work.
D05-04.example: Example: Sibiya Grill House in Soweto files the gas practitioner registration and installation certificate for its new LPG cooking line.
common_gaps: A practitioner registered for a different gas type or category
No certificate after a cylinder bank was moved

what_to_submit: Copy of the explosives licence or blasting certificate held by each person handling explosives
Magazine or storage licence where you store explosives
Licence expiry dates
D05-05.why: Explosives are tightly controlled because misuse can kill many people at once, so only licensed or certificated people may handle, store or use them. Check each licence before any work and keep copies current.
D05-05.example: Example: Themba Quarrying near Kuruman files the blasting certificate of its blaster, Andile Mokoena, and the licence for its explosives magazine.
common_gaps: Assistants handling explosives without the certificate or direct supervision the rules require
Storage licence not renewed when the magazine moved

what_to_submit: Firearm competency certificate for each person who carries a firearm at work
Firearm licence for each company firearm and the register of who holds it
Record of regular practical shooting or proficiency training
D05-06.why: An armed person without proven competence is a danger to themselves and the public, and firearms law requires competency for each firearm type. Check competency before issuing a firearm and keep records current.
D05-06.example: Example: Ngubane Armed Response in Richards Bay files the competency certificate for each armed officer next to the firearm issue register.
common_gaps: Issuing a firearm type the person is not certified for
No record of who held which firearm on which shift

what_to_submit: PSIRA registration certificate for each security officer, showing their grade
Company's PSIRA registration as a security service provider
Date you last checked each registration was active
D05-07.why: The private security industry is regulated under the PSIRA regime, so every officer must be registered at a grade that matches the post they fill. Clients often check this before a contract starts.
D05-07.example: Example: Mokoena Guarding in Klerksdorp files PSIRA certificates for its 18 officers and checks that the site supervisor holds the grade the client contract asks for.
common_gaps: Officers placed on posts above their registered grade
Registrations lapsed because fees were not paid

what_to_submit: Lead examination outcome per exposed worker: fit, fit with restrictions or unfit
The Plan's lead protocol and exposure group list
E06-01.why: The Lead Regulations expect exposed workers to be under medical surveillance, because lead builds up in the body and harms the nerves, kidneys and unborn children. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-01.example: Example: Govender Battery Recyclers in Pietermaritzburg files the lead fitness outcome for each smelter worker; the laboratory results stay with the occupational health practitioner.
common_gaps: Filing blood lead results in the File
Not moving a worker when the OMP says unfit for lead work

what_to_submit: Asbestos examination outcome per person exposed to asbestos
Link to the asbestos work plan or abatement contract
Exit examination outcome when the person leaves asbestos work, where the Plan sets one
E06-02.why: Asbestos diseases appear many years after exposure, so people who work with it are examined as the Plan and the OMP set, often including when they leave the work. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-02.example: Example: Petersen Demolition in Kraaifontein files asbestos fitness outcomes for its removal team before stripping roof sheets from an old factory.
common_gaps: No exit examination when the Plan calls for one
Contractors' teams working without outcomes on file

what_to_submit: Hazardous chemical agent examination outcome per exposed worker
The Plan protocol linked to your chemical risk assessment
E06-03.why: The Hazardous Chemical Agents Regulations call for medical surveillance where the risk assessment shows a chemical may harm health, so early changes are picked up before disease sets in. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-03.example: Example: Mbatha Paints in Chloorkop files fitness outcomes for its mixers exposed to solvents, as set out in its Plan.
common_gaps: Surveillance for chemicals that are no longer used, while new ones are missed

what_to_submit: Hazardous biological agent examination outcome per exposed worker
Record that vaccination was offered to each exposed worker, with the date; whether the worker accepted or declined stays with the occupational health practitioner
The Plan protocol linked to your biological risk assessment
E06-04.why: The Hazardous Biological Agents Regulations call for surveillance of people exposed to germs at work, such as healthcare, laboratory, waste and sewage workers. Clinical records, including vaccination status and whether a worker accepted or declined a vaccination, stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-04.example: Example: Nxumalo Veterinary Clinic in Vryheid files fitness outcomes for its animal handlers and a dated record that each was offered the vaccinations its practitioner recommends.
common_gaps: Keeping vaccination cards with clinical details in the File

what_to_submit: Hearing examination outcome per worker in a noise zone: baseline, periodic and exit
The Plan's noise protocol and noise zone list
Evidence that the testing was done by a competent person with suitable equipment
E06-05.why: Hearing loss from noise is permanent, so baseline and follow up tests show whether your controls are working and protect you in a later compensation claim. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-05.example: Example: Dlamini Sawmills in Sabie files baseline hearing outcomes for new mill staff and an exit outcome for each person who leaves.
common_gaps: No baseline test, so later loss cannot be measured
Audiograms filed instead of the outcome

what_to_submit: Radiation worker examination outcome per worker
The radiation licence conditions that set the examination
Link to the dose monitoring records kept by the radiation protection officer
E06-06.why: People who work with X ray units or radioactive sources must be fit for that work and monitored, as the radiation control authority's licence conditions set. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-06.example: Example: Sebego Radiology in Mahikeng files the fitness outcome for each radiographer, with dose records kept separately by its radiation protection officer.
common_gaps: Mixing personal dose results into the medical outcome file

what_to_submit: Fitness for work at height outcome per person on the fall protection plan
Link to the working at height training record in Section D
E06-07.why: A dizzy spell or an uncontrolled medical condition can turn a slip at height into a fatal fall, so the Construction Regulations, 2014 expect people who work at height to be certified fit for it. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-07.example: Example: Zwane Roofing in Kempton Park sends its two new roofers for a work at height fitness assessment before their first day on the roof, and files both fit outcomes.
common_gaps: Assuming a general certificate covers work at height when it does not say so

what_to_submit: Fitness for confined space work outcome per entrant and standby person
Link to the confined space training in Section D
E06-08.why: Confined spaces are hot, cramped and may need breathing apparatus, so entrants and rescuers must be fit enough to work and get out safely. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-08.example: Example: Hlongwane Water Services in Emalahleni files confined space fitness outcomes for its reservoir team, including the standby rescuer.
common_gaps: Standby rescuers never assessed

what_to_submit: Night work health assessment outcome per regular night worker
Record of any move to day work the OMP recommended
E06-09.why: Regular night work can affect health, and employment law gives night workers protection, including access to a health assessment; your Plan sets how you handle it. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-09.example: Example: Moodley Bakeries in Chatsworth files night work fitness outcomes for its night shift bakers and moves one to day shift on the OMP's advice.
common_gaps: No assessment offered to long term night workers

what_to_submit: Food handler fitness outcome per food handler
Your illness reporting and exclusion procedure, and a record of the dates a food handler was excluded and cleared to return, without the illness
E06-10.why: Food handlers who are ill can spread infection to customers, so they must be fit to handle food and report illness before a shift. Clinical records stay with the occupational health practitioner; only the outcome (fit, fit with restrictions or unfit) goes in your File.
E06-10.example: Example: Mabuza Catering in Mbombela files a fit to handle food outcome for each cook and a record of the dates a cook was kept off shift and cleared to return, with the reason kept by its practitioner.
common_gaps: Filing medical notes for sick leave instead of the outcome
